inputs.text: They want everyone to see Harry Wait as the villain and stop at the verdict: two misdemeanor convictions and one felony identity-theft conviction, with another identity-theft count rejected. But the point he raised—that he requested ballots for Robin Vos and Cory Mason to expose weaknesses in Wisconsin’s voter-registration system—gets buried under the fraud label. That looks less like accountability than a warning to anyone who tests the system: challenge its safeguards and the institutions will make you the story. Calling his group false-claimers only helps protect the system from scrutiny, and leaves unanswered who benefits when its vulnerabilities are ignored.
